correctness.rationale: The dual is correctly defined by the absence of disconnected four-subsets. The five-regular graph has 680 connected quadruples and 192 induced pentagons; all smaller dual faces are present and no six-faces occur. A standalone exact integer verifier constructs the signed boundaries and proves d3*d4=0. The full two-skeleton has a canonical free rank-455 2-cycle lattice. Unit-pivot integer elimination produces surjective d3 of rank 455 and primitive d4 of rank 191; no torsion is concealed by rational ranks. The two-connected three-skeleton is a wedge of 225 three-spheres, and primitive d4 attachments cancel 191 of them to leave 34 three-spheres and one four-sphere. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality on 16 vertices puts Z in cut homology degree 9 and Z^34 in degree 10, and proves the original pure dimension-11 complex nonshellable.

value.rationale: This exact finite example is a natural transition from the Boolean four-cube to its 5-regular antipodal augmentation, and distinguishes ordinary from total cuts. Its 192 induced pentagons generate a genuine degree-four dual sphere alongside 34 degree-three spheres, while the original pure dimension-eleven complex acquires two separate non-top free homology degrees. The same graph at ordinary k=3 and total k=4 has known torsion; therefore the integral torsion-free classification at ordinary k=4 gives a mathematically meaningful boundary, beyond a routine scalar count. The standalone exact calculation is not an unmotivated slice.
